 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Kimi Antonelli starts from pole position Sunday at the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix, one strong result from moving closer to his first drivers' championship.
 The race covers 56 laps over roughly 308 kilometers, according to Formula 1, at Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas. The green flag drops at 3 p.m. CDT.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Antonelli took pole with a 1:34.035 lap, according to Pitpass, his seventh of the season. He holds a 102-point lead over Russell in the standings. Russell, his Mercedes teammate, starts sixth.

 How to Watch the United States Grand Prix Sunday
 Here are the race's start times by country — 3 p.m. CDT in Austin, 1 p.m. PDT and 4 p.m. EDT across the United States, 8 p.m. GMT in the United Kingdom and 9 p.m. CET in both Italy and Germany.
 In the United States, Apple TV holds exclusive rights, with no traditional linear broadcast, according to MacObserver . Practice sessions streamed free in the app, but the race generally requires an Apple TV subscription, which includes F1 TV Premium.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the United Kingdom, Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event carry the race live at 8 p.m. GMT, according to Sky Sports , with coverage typically beginning at 6:30 p.m. Sky customers can stream on Sky Go, while NOW offers day passes and monthly memberships. Channel 4 airs free highlights only. F1 TV Pro does not offer live races there because of Sky's exclusive rights.
 In Italy, Sky Sport F1 on channel 207, Sky Sport Uno on 201 and Sky Sport 4K on 213 show the race live at 9 p.m. CET, according to La Repubblica . Streaming runs on Sky Go and NOW. TV8 airs a free delayed broadcast at 10:30 p.m., and its website, tv8.it, carries the same feed.
 In Germany, Sky Sport F1 airs the race live in German at 9 p.m. CET, with build-up starting around 7 p.m., according to Formel1.de . WOW streams the race, and Sky Go serves subscribers. RTL showed qualifying free, but the race is not available free live.

 United States Grand Prix Starting Grid and Standings
 Max Verstappen starts second for Red Bull, with teammate Isack Hadjar third, according to The Race . Ferrari's Charles Leclerc is fourth and Lewis Hamilton fifth, while Russell lines up sixth. McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris follow in seventh and eighth.
 Liam Lawson, Pierre Gasly and Nico Hulkenberg start ninth through 11th, and Fernando Alonso is 12th. Oliver Bearman is 13th for Haas, followed by Lindblad, Esteban Ocon, Lance Stroll, Carlos Sainz, Alex Albon, Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas, with Colapinto 21st and Bortoleto 22nd.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Arvid Lindblad of Racing Bulls serves a five-place penalty and Franco Colapinto of Alpine a 10-place penalty, while Gabriel Bortoleto of Audi faces a penalty of roughly 60 places, according to Crash.net .
 Antonelli leads the drivers' standings with 340 points after 17 rounds, according to RacingNews365 . Russell has 238, Hamilton 229, Verstappen 221 and Leclerc 215. Hamilton sits nine points behind Russell for second place, and Verstappen is eight points behind Hamilton. Norris sits sixth with 201, followed by Piastri with 138, Hadjar with 97, Lawson with 75 and Gasly with 41.
 Antonelli can clinch his first title Sunday with a victory if Russell finishes ninth or lower, though results involving Hamilton and others also factor in.
 Mercedes leads the constructors' standings with 578 points, ahead of Ferrari at 444, McLaren at 339 and Red Bull at 332, according to RacingNews365. That gap over Ferrari is 134 points. Racing Bulls (100), Alpine (68), Haas (30), Audi (23), Williams (12), Aston Martin (7) and Cadillac (0) complete the field.
